A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVLM-Count. All 31 pages of v2 and 38 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable matching of methods, tables, figures, and relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original counting experiments on FSC-147, TallyQA, PASCAL VOC, and Emoji-Count, together with ablations and qualitative application results.

after.justification: v3 reports original counting experiments, including Penguin benchmark results, detector-removal ablations, visual-exemplar and prompting experiments, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The core pipeline, mean-shift division-point selection, and A* routing remain unchanged. v3 adds a SAM-only variant bypassing GroundingDINO and adaptations using visual exemplars or combined text/exemplar inputs (Appendices A, D, L). Mask erosion and polishing are newly documented, but this alone does not establish their absence from the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: v3 removes the TallyQA counting evaluation covering 155 simple and 149 complex questions, while retaining its answer-distribution illustration. It extends the previously illustrated penguin application to a systematic benchmark and adds exemplar-only and combined text/exemplar input scenarios on Emoji-Count. FSC-147, PASCAL VOC, Emoji-Count, and the other application domains remain.

E2.justification: Gemini 1.5 Pro is replaced by Gemma 3 27B. v3 adds GPT-4o counting segmentation masks as a comparator on FSC-147, VOC, and Emoji-Count, and adds DAVEprm to the VOC and Emoji comparisons. CounTX and the untrained GroundingREC entry disappear from FSC-147. Most dedicated-counter comparisons are retained in Appendix K.

E3.justification: The stated FSC-147 prompt drops the instruction to answer zero when no targets appear. v3 introduces a 100-image, frequency-balanced Penguin evaluation using the separate-site split and maximum annotator count as ground truth. It revises the FSC-147 plot intervals and adds exemplar, CoT, and 1,000-image timing protocols. The prompt revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds detector-removal tests, occlusion and mask-post-processing case studies, a crowded FSC-147 subset analysis, and exemplar/CoT comparisons. The existing count-range analysis is revised. Appendix A retains the stage ablations but removes Gemini experiments and adds a SAM-only condition. The earlier FSC-147 annotation-error case study is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three trials in Figure 2 and the Table 1 caption. No changed seed disclosure, confidence intervals, error-bar practice, or significance testing is evident. New result rows and timing averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: LVLM-Count/GPT-4o MAE changes from 19.24 to 18.09 on FSC-147 and from 14.97 to 16.29 on Emoji-Count. GroundingREC's Emoji MAE changes from 36.16 to 143.22. Extensive Penguin, Gemma, prompting, and timing results are added. These are revised reports with accompanying setting changes, not established same-setting gains. v3 Table 3 gives a Qwen2 RMSE improvement of 143.84, whereas Table 16 correctly gives 146.28.

T1.justification: The graph construction, path-finding formulation, and division-point mathematics are retained. Accuracy definitions match between v2 Table 6 and v3 Table 7. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift from broad superiority and generalization claims against dedicated counting methods to evaluating LVLM weaknesses and providing a baseline for improving large-count performance. LVLM evaluation becomes an explicit main contribution. Training-free operation and the object-aware-division contribution remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of detector independence, tolerance of false positives, and post-processing for occlusion. It adds interpretations of runtime overhead and a limitation concerning structured numerical outputs from open-source models. The zero-prediction limitation remains, while TallyQA-specific interpretations and the FSC-147 annotation-error discussion are removed.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the detection threshold of 0.1, two-pixel mask separation, erosion/polishing details, SAM-only configuration, output-formatting and regex guidance, and exemplar/CoT instructions. Appendix J documents stage timings and parallel sub-image queries. These substantially expand implementation information; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts toward LVLM assessment and enhancement, with dedicated counting models framed as reference points in Appendix K. A new related-work discussion cites LVLM evaluations by Yin, Xu, and Yang. Gemma 3 and CoT references are added, while Gemini and Claude references are removed. The object-aware-division novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and results narrative are substantially rewritten around the revised research emphasis. The conclusion is replaced by a Limitations section. Appendices are reorganized with a new contents page and several new thematic sections, while much of the method exposition and application discussion is retained.

P2.justification: v3 restructures the main comparison tables and redisplays dedicated-counter comparisons in the appendix. It adds robustness, timing, exemplar, and CoT tables and crowded-scene figures, removes TallyQA and annotation-error illustrations, and revises the count-range plots from two to three panels with different axes and intervals. Many workflow and application images remain identical.

improvement.justification: v3 offers better-calibrated claims and stronger evidence about detector dependence and crowded scenes (Table 4; Appendices A, C-D), plus useful implementation and timing information absent from v2. These improve the central proposal's support and practical reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removing TallyQA and Gemini evaluations and introducing the inconsistent Qwen2 RMSE improvement reported in Tables 3 and 16.
